name: The White Roads
summary: Remnants of the Concord's white paved roads, which once ran continent-wide. Pulled up for firewood during the Falling Kingdoms; purge convoys later used the stumps as route-markers. Sections survive in the Wealdmark and the Ashlands — and walking them at dusk is considered either luck or an invitation.

geography.character: bone-pale paving stones, stump-lines where the road was quarried away, mile-markers carved with Weaver script (illegal to copy)

notable_sections.name: The Wealdmark Stumps
notable_sections.note: The best surviving stretch: a full mile of stumped roadbed through orchard country.

notable_sections.name: The Ashland Causeway
notable_sections.note: A raised white section crossing ash-marsh; it predates the Quiet and refuses to sink.

lore_notes: Reading the mile-marker script aloud is forbidden by Septuary regulation rather than Crown law — an oddity that has never been explained.
Salvage crews prize the paving: Concord stone takes no weather and rings true under a hammer.
adventure_hooks: A causeway section that was broken for a century is found repaired overnight.
A stump-line leads somewhere new this season — the old road is showing a detour around something.
